description: #5259 — positional undo stops at a page's BIRTH. `create_page_in_space` appends two ops in one transaction — the root's own `create_block` and its first `set_property(space)` — and page creation pushes no frontend undo entry, so a Ctrl+Z past the page's content fell through to `undo_page_group`, whose walk seeded on those two and reverted them: a soft-deleted root left open as a blank page, or (undoing the space assignment alone) a page in no space at all. Both enumeration queries now exclude the root's `create_block` and its first `set_property(space)` from the row universe (`find_positional_undo_target`, `enumerate_undo_group_in_tx`), so the first undo reverts the typing alone — the window here is wide enough to have swallowed all three — and the next positional undo, at the depth the frontend advanced to, refuses with `not_found` rather than reaching the birth (the empty group `undo_page_group` answers there is pinned by `page_undo_stops_at_the_pages_birth_5259`; a `[]` return is not a record the #3083 ratchet accepts). The settled snapshot is the evidence: the page row keeps `deleted_at: null`, the typed block is a tombstone, and the digest holds ONE reverse op, not three.
name: undo_page_birth

ops.comment: The space the page is born in, named `C1` by its `create_block`.
ops.name: a_space_to_be_born_in

ops.comment: The birth: `create_block` for the root (`C2`) and its first `set_property(space)`, in one transaction and so inside any undo window.
ops.name: the_page_is_born

ops.comment: What the user typed after creating the page — the only op a Ctrl+Z should reach.
The window swallows every op this fixture made, so without the exclusion the group is THREE rows ending in the root's own create — the page trashed. With it, one row: the typing.
ops.name: ctrl_z_undoes_the_typing_only

ops.comment: The single-op positional path shares the row universe: past the content there is no op at depth 1, so it refuses rather than reaching the birth.
ops.name: single_positional_undo_refuses_past_the_content
